questions.question: Which of these is a narrative technique?
options: Point of view
Alphabetical order
Page numbering
Font size
questions.explanation: Point of view — who tells the story — is one of the most fundamental narrative techniques, along with foreshadowing and time structure.

questions.question: What is an unreliable narrator?
options: A narrator whose account cannot be fully trusted
A narrator who speaks several languages
A narrator who is not named
A narrator who only appears at the end
questions.explanation: An unreliable narrator gives an account the reader cannot fully trust, forcing us to read critically between the lines.

questions.question: What is foreshadowing?
options: Hints early in a story about what will happen later
A summary at the end of a chapter
Describing shadows in the setting
Starting the story with the ending
questions.explanation: Foreshadowing plants hints about future events, building tension and making the ending feel earned.

questions.question: Why does identifying narrative techniques improve your literary analysis?
options: You can explain HOW the story creates its effects, not just what happens
It lets you skip reading the text
It guarantees a top grade automatically
It replaces the need for quotes
questions.explanation: Recognising how a story is told lets you analyse the author's deliberate choices instead of just summarising the plot.

questions.question: How do narrative techniques help you as a writer?
options: You can make deliberate choices about who tells your story and how time is organised
They remove the need for planning
They only matter in poetry
They make stories shorter
questions.explanation: Knowing the techniques lets you make conscious choices about point of view, structure and information in your own creative texts.
